slides.subline: It is not a house rule. Korean law sorts every place that feeds you into six licence types, and one line decides which

slides.label: categories cover every business in Korea that cooks and serves you something. Which one a cafe filed under decides what it is allowed to pour

slides.title:
The split is not
about the food.
slides.body:
The decree does not sort these businesses by what they cook. Several of the six cook much the same things. It sorts them by whether drinking is allowed on the premises.

A 휴게음식점, the category most cafes file under, is defined as serving tea, ice cream or fast-food and snack-bar fare, and as a business 'where drinking is not permitted'. A 일반음식점 covers the same cooking but is one 'where drinking is incidentally permitted alongside meals'. 제과점, the bakery licence, is a no-drinking category too.

So a cafe that wants wine on the menu does not add a permit. It has to become a different kind of business.

slides.cta:
We read the decree so you don't have to.
Save this before your next coffee

caption:
Ask for a beer in a Korean cafe and you will often be told no. It is rarely a house rule. It is usually the licence on the wall.

Korea's Food Sanitation Act Enforcement Decree, article 21(8), sorts every business that cooks and serves food into six categories. What surprises people is that the dividing line is not the food. Several of the six cook much the same things. The line is whether drinking is allowed on the premises.

A 휴게음식점 — the rest-type category most cafes file under — is defined as serving tea, ice cream, fast food and snack-bar fare, and as a business where drinking is not permitted. A 일반음식점, the general restaurant category, covers the same cooking but is one where drinking is permitted incidentally alongside a meal. 제과점, the bakery licence, is also a no-drinking category. The other three are 단란주점, 유흥주점 and 위탁급식 — contract catering inside someone else's canteen.

So a cafe that wants wine on the list does not bolt on a permit. It has to be a different kind of business. That is why the natural-wine place pouring at midnight is, on paper, a restaurant whatever its sign says. And note the decree's wording: 음주행위, the act of drinking, not the sale. Bringing your own bottle into a rest-type cafe is not a loophole, because the category is about what may happen in the room.

One genuinely useful side effect for visitors: any rest-type or general food business of 150m² or more must display a price list outside the shop as well as inside, with prices shown VAT-included. If a larger place has no prices on the door, that is worth noticing.

A change is coming but has not arrived. In July 2026 the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety pre-announced an amendment letting cafes, restaurants and bakeries switch between the three categories with a change filing instead of closing and re-registering, cutting the fee from 28,000 won to 9,300. As of 4 November 2026 it is still a proposal, not law.

Sources in the last slide. Research, not a visit, and no venue recommended here.
